title: 9.8 million families poor, 5.8 million experienced hunger – OCTA
summary: Self-rated poverty hardly moved in the third quarter of the year, with an estimated 9.8 million Filipino families rating themselves poor, a survey by the OCTA Research group showed.

blocks.text: From 39 percent in July, self-rated poverty was at 37 percent in the latest survey conducted from Sept. 28 to Oct. 4.

MANILA, Philippines — Self-rated poverty hardly moved in the third quarter of the year, with an estimated 9.8 million Filipino families rating themselves poor, a survey by the OCTA Research group showed.
OCTA said this translates to an estimated 9.8 million poor families, from approximately 10.3 million in the previous survey.
Those who said their families were not poor increased from 18 percent to 21 percent, while those who can’t say if their families are poor or not remained at 42 percent.

Like in previous polls, self-rated poverty was highest among those in Mindanao at 56 percent (from 58 percent), followed by those in the Visayas at 49 percent (from 46 percent), balance Luzon at 26 percent (from 33 percent) and Metro Manila at 20 percent (from 18 percent).
“The Q3 results show national self-rated poverty holding at the elevated level reached in Q2; the two-point difference is within the margin of error and should not be read as a decline,” OCTA said.

“The persistently high incidence in Mindanao and among Class E households underscores the continued vulnerability of lower-income families and the need for targeted measures that strengthen household incomes, employment stability and protection against rising living costs,” it added.
The latest poll also showed almost similar hunger incidence rate from the previous quarter, from 21 percent to 22 percent.
OCTA said this translates to an estimated 5.8 million families, from 5.6 million in July.
Meanwhile, 78 percent said they did not experience hunger in the past three months, from 79 percent.

Across areas, hunger incidence was highest among those in the Visayas and Metro Manila at 29 percent (from 17 percent and 19 percent, respectively), followed by those in rest of Luzon at 21 percent (from 27 percent) and Mindanao at 16 percent (from 14 percent).
“These results show that the steady national figure conceals different patterns across the country. The increases in NCR and the Visayas contrast with the decline in balance Luzon,” OCTA said.
The survey had 1,200 respondents and a margin of error of plus/minus three percent.
